steps.name: dataset
steps.label: Reference data
steps.says: Reads a named data set beside the items: FX rates, a budget, limits, prior periods.

steps.name: derive
steps.label: Computed fields
steps.says: Adds fields computed from each item, the case and policy (age, ratios, flags).

steps.name: filter
steps.label: Filter
steps.says: Keeps the items that match; the others stay on the case, marked with the reason.

steps.name: convert
steps.label: Currency conversion
steps.says: Converts amounts to one currency with the case's own rates; a missing rate is flagged, never assumed.

steps.name: bucket
steps.label: Bands
steps.says: Puts each item in a band of a field: ageing 0–1 day, 2–5 days…; size; service level.

steps.name: dedupe
steps.label: Duplicates
steps.says: Finds items with the same key fields; duplicates are set aside (kept on the case) or marked.

steps.name: aggregate
steps.label: Roll up
steps.says: Rolls items up by key fields with totals and counts — into the items, or into a data set.

steps.name: transform
steps.label: Team logic (tool)
steps.says: Sends the items to the team's own tool and uses what it returns — for logic expressions cannot hold.

steps.name: recompute
steps.label: Recompute and compare
steps.says: Recalculates a figure (fees, interest, accruals) by formula or the team's tool and compares it to what was booked.

steps.name: schedule
steps.label: Schedule over periods
steps.says: Spreads each item's amount over periods (prepayments, accrual release, leases) into a data set.

steps.name: propose_entries
steps.label: Journal entries
steps.says: Drafts balanced journals for the groups that need them; an unbalanced entry, an unknown account or no period is caught before anyone sees it.

steps.name: period_check
steps.label: Period open?
steps.says: Stops the run (to a person) if the accounting period is closed or locked for the entity.

steps.name: post
steps.label: Post journals
steps.says: Posts the approved journals to the ledger after a second person releases them — the ledger's own check first; each journal once, however often retried.

steps.name: flux
steps.label: Change over periods
steps.says: Compares each item with its own history: change, % change and how unusual (z-score).

steps.name: anomaly
steps.label: Unusual against history
steps.says: Flags items far from their own history (z-score above a threshold) — statistics, no model.

steps.name: consistency
steps.label: Consistency checks
steps.says: Checks totals across data sets (sub-ledger = GL, report A = report B); each failing check becomes an item to investigate.

steps.name: sample
steps.label: Sample
steps.says: Selects a reproducible sample (random, largest, or by value; stratified; some always included); the rest stay on the case, marked.

steps.name: score
steps.label: Risk score
steps.says: Adds a weighted score from named factors, its reasons and a band (high / medium / low) that review lanes and approvals can use.

steps.name: attest
steps.label: Owner attestation
steps.says: An owner certifies a statement (an account, a control, a report) at a tollgate; recorded with who, when, evidence and expiry.

steps.name: await
steps.label: Wait for an event
steps.says: The run waits here for an event (a reply, a confirmation, a file) or for its child cases, with a timeout.

steps.name: spawn
steps.label: Child cases
steps.says: Opens a child case per item (per account, per sample, per client) in a capability; an `await` for `children` then rolls their outcomes up.

steps.name: report
steps.label: Report
steps.says: Writes the case's report (configuration, findings, decisions, data used, sign-off) as a PDF kept with the case.

steps.name: compose
steps.label: Draft a message
steps.says: Drafts the outbound message per group (client reply, counterparty query) for the reviewer; it is sent only by an approved `outreach` or write-back.

steps.name: match_n
steps.label: Match several systems
steps.says: Matches two or more systems by key (e.g. purchase order, goods receipt, invoice), with many-to-one sums; keeps what does not agree.

steps.name: intake
steps.label: File intake
steps.says: Reads a file (a workbook from the documents service) into items with a column map and checks; rows that fail are kept aside, with why.

steps.name: extract
steps.label: Read a document
steps.says: Reads fields from a document (patterns first, then the model); every value must appear in the document, and low-confidence or regulated values go to a person.

steps.name: clock
steps.label: Clocks
steps.says: Starts service-level or regulatory clocks per item (hours or business days, paused for time waiting on the client); people are warned before and told on breach.

steps.name: timeline
steps.label: Timeline
steps.says: Builds one ordered timeline of events from several systems for the reviewer (and the model).

steps.name: link
steps.label: Related cases
steps.says: Finds earlier cases about the same client, account or counterparty (any capability) and shows how they ended.

steps.name: screen
steps.label: Name screening (candidates)
steps.says: Fuzzy-matches names against a list and marks candidate matches for a person; it never clears or confirms a match.

steps.name: outreach
steps.label: Send to the other party
steps.says: Sends each drafted message (client, counterparty, another team) through the bank's channel, after a person approves sending at the tollgate before it.

reasoning.skill:
You are a senior Product Controller investigating FOBO breaks on the CATS
(front office) vs MOTIF (back office) reconciliation. You do not guess, you
do not default to posting, and you do not stop at the first plausible
explanation. The objective is to restore FO PnL = BO PnL + FOBO adjustments
truthfully; plugging an adjustment to force it is a failure.

What you receive has already been through the playbook: every break carries
its cause checks, its validation tests (FO-1…FO-8, BO-1…BO-6: pass, fail or
not run, and why), FO-6 findings, category and side. You only see what the
playbook could not settle: judgement categories (corporate action, novel,
aged, missing side, adjustments that did not clear) and breaks whose side is
not proven. Use the tools for the rest: MOTIF booking events, MB Rec break
history, and CATS and MOTIF trades for the trade-level step (§7: when FO and
BO both appear correct but the break persists, validate every trade for
quantity, direction, consideration, price, pull factor and settlement).

Rules you never break:
- A break is a symptom, not an instruction to post (R1).
- Never assume FO is correct; validate FO before BO (R2). A cause that
  originates in FO is never posted.
- Decompose by component; never reason about aggregate PnL (R3).
- Identify the truth before the adjustment (R4).
- If you cannot evidence it, escalate it (R6). A plausible cause is a
  hypothesis: say what evidence would confirm it.
- Do not post by elimination: "BO passed" is not evidence of a genuine break.
- Price = 0 may be a valid corporate action; do not conclude without evidence.
- Never invent a threshold (P1). If a conclusion depends on an unset
  threshold, say so and give the conclusion conditionally.
- Judgement breaks are recommendations for SME review, not assertions (R7).
- Weigh what the controller wrote at the tollgate (e.g. the desk's view) as
  context, but cite figures only from the tools or the breaks.

Answer in the sections you are given (the skill's §12 output). The break

reasoning.skill:
You are a senior Product Controller investigating FOBO breaks on the CATS
(front office) vs MOTIF (back office) reconciliation for Rates books.
Check curve datasets and fixings first: most Rates breaks are a curve or
fixing taken at a different time. You do not guess, you
do not default to posting, and you do not stop at the first plausible
explanation. The objective is to restore FO PnL = BO PnL + FOBO adjustments
truthfully; plugging an adjustment to force it is a failure.

What you receive has already been through the playbook: every break carries
its cause checks, its validation tests (FO-1…FO-8, BO-1…BO-6: pass, fail or
not run, and why), FO-6 findings, category and side. You only see what the
playbook could not settle: judgement categories (corporate action, novel,
aged, missing side, adjustments that did not clear) and breaks whose side is
not proven. Use the tools for the rest: MOTIF booking events, MB Rec break
history, and CATS and MOTIF trades for the trade-level step (§7: when FO and
BO both appear correct but the break persists, validate every trade for
quantity, direction, consideration, price, pull factor and settlement).

Rules you never break:
- A break is a symptom, not an instruction to post (R1).
- Never assume FO is correct; validate FO before BO (R2). A cause that
  originates in FO is never posted.
- Decompose by component; never reason about aggregate PnL (R3).
- Identify the truth before the adjustment (R4).
- If you cannot evidence it, escalate it (R6). A plausible cause is a
  hypothesis: say what evidence would confirm it.
- Do not post by elimination: "BO passed" is not evidence of a genuine break.
- Price = 0 may be a valid corporate action; do not conclude without evidence.
- Never invent a threshold (P1). If a conclusion depends on an unset
  threshold, say so and give the conclusion conditionally.
- Judgement breaks are recommendations for SME review, not assertions (R7).
- Weigh what the controller wrote at the tollgate (e.g. the desk's view) as
  context, but cite figures only from the tools or the breaks.

body.name: Close sign-off and attestation (template)
body.description: Check every close control's evidence, explain exceptions, owners attest, publish the attestation.
body.yaml:
# Template — close sign-off & attestation: each close control's evidence is
# checked, exceptions are explained, owners attest, and an attestation PDF is
# published. `controls.checklist` is a placeholder: onboard your close-controls
# connector (or point the load at an existing tool) and the validator will pass.
id: team.close-attestation
name: Close sign-off and attestation (template)
description: Check every close control's evidence, explain exceptions, owners attest, publish the attestation.
owners: { people: [], role: YOUR_OWNER_ROLE, four_eyes: true }
case:
  label: Close
  item_label: Control
  key: [entity, period]
  subject: "{entity} close · {period}"
  scopes: { entity: entity }
  opens_on: schedule
  schedule: "0 8 3 * *"
  schedule_keys: [{ entity: YOUR_ENTITY, period: "{prev_month}" }]
  opens_as: YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT
items:
  load: { tool: controls.checklist, args: { entity: $case.entity, period: $case.period } }
  id_field: control_id
  display: [control_id, control, owner, status, evidence]
  in_scope: status != 'passed'
steps: [load, group, reason, draft, validate, review, record, publish]
pause_before: [review, publish]
group_by: [owner]
rules:
  - id: evidence-missing
    when: count >= 1
    then: { status: escalated, comment: "{count} control(s) without passing evidence for {owner}.", reason: EVIDENCE_MISSING }
reasoning: { reasoner: none }
review: { roles: [YOUR_CONTROL_OWNER_ROLE] }
publish:
  tool: documents.render_pdf_report
  per: case
  args: { entity: $case.entity, name: $case_id, title: Close attestation, subtitle: $subject,
          sections: $approved, sign_off: $sign_off }
  approver_roles: [YOUR_FINANCIAL_CONTROLLER_ROLE]
retention: { days: 2555 }

body.name: Variance commentary (template)
body.description: Commentary on material variances to plan, written back after a four-eyes release.
body.yaml:
# Template — variance commentary: load actuals and plan, keep the material lines,
# explain each, sign off, publish to the reporting pack after a second release.
id: team.variance-commentary
name: Variance commentary (template)
description: Commentary on material variances to plan, written back after a four-eyes release.
owners: { people: [], role: YOUR_OWNER_ROLE, four_eyes: true }
case:
  label: Lane
  item_label: Variance line
  key: [entity, period]
  subject: "{entity} · {period}"
  scopes: { entity: entity }
items:
  load: { tool: gl.balances, args: { entity: $case.entity, period: $case.period } }
  id_field: line_id
  amount_field: variance
  display: [account, account_name, cost_centre, actual, budget, variance]
  in_scope: abs(variance) >= policy.materiality
compare: { measure: actual, baseline: budget, as: variance }
policy:
  materiality: { value: 50000, unit: GBP }
steps: [load, compare, group, reason, draft, validate, review, record, publish]
pause_before: [review, publish]
group_by: [account]
reasoning:
  reasoner: llm
  output: commentary
  tools: [gl.journal_lines, budget.plan_lines]
  skill: |
    Explain each material variance to plan for a finance reviewer from the
    journal lines and plan notes. Cite only figures from the tools or the lines.
review: { roles: [YOUR_PREPARER_ROLE, YOUR_REVIEWER_ROLE] }
publish:
  tool: reporting.publish_commentary
  args: { entity: $case.entity, period: $case.period, account: $group.account, commentary: $comment }
  approver_roles: [YOUR_REVIEWER_ROLE]
limits: { max_cost_usd_per_case: 5 }
retention: { days: 2555 }

body.name: Reconciliation (template)
body.description: Match two systems on a key, explain every break with rules then the model, sign off.
body.yaml:
# Template — reconciliation: match two systems, explain every break, sign off.
# Replace the ids, tools, keys and roles; the validator lists anything left.
id: team.reconciliation
name: Reconciliation (template)
description: Match two systems on a key, explain every break with rules then the model, sign off.
owners: { people: [], role: YOUR_OWNER_ROLE, four_eyes: true }
case:
  label: Rec run
  item_label: Break
  key: [entity, date]
  subject: "{entity} · {date}"
  scopes: { entity: entity }
items:
  id_field: item_id
  amount_field: difference
  display: [ref, break_type, left_amount, right_amount, difference]
match:
  left: { tool: bank.statement, args: { entity: $case.entity, date: $case.date } }
  right: { tool: ledger.postings, args: { entity: $case.entity, date: $case.date } }
  keys: [ref]
  amount_field: amount
  tolerance: 0.01
  left_label: left
  right_label: right
policy:
  write_off_limit: { value: 100, unit: GBP }
steps: [match, group, reason, draft, validate, review, record]
group_by: [break_type]
rules:
  - id: small-break
    when: count == 1 and abs(total) <= policy.write_off_limit
    then: { status: proposed, comment: "One difference of {total}, within the write-off limit; propose write-off." }
reasoning:
  reasoner: llm
  tools: [ledger.counterparty_history]
  skill: |
    You investigate reconciliation breaks between two systems. Find the likely
    cause of each group of breaks and the next action. Cite only figures from
    the tools or the breaks; escalate when nothing explains a difference.
review: { roles: [YOUR_REVIEWER_ROLE] }
retention: { days: 2555 }

body.name: Report validation (template)
body.description: Check a management report line by line against the ledger; publish a PDF validation report.
body.yaml:
# Template — report validation: check a report (Excel) against the ledger and
# publish a PDF validation report.
id: team.report-validation
name: Report validation (template)
description: Check a management report line by line against the ledger; publish a PDF validation report.
owners: { people: [], role: YOUR_OWNER_ROLE, four_eyes: true }
case:
  label: Validation
  item_label: Report line
  key: [entity, period, report]
  subject: "{report} · {entity} · {period}"
  scopes: { entity: entity }
items:
  id_field: item_id
  amount_field: difference
  display: [account, cost_centre, report_amount, ledger_amount, difference, break_type]
match:
  left: { tool: documents.read_workbook, args: { entity: $case.entity, name: $case.report } }
  right: { tool: gl.balances, args: { entity: $case.entity, period: $case.period } }
  keys: [account, cost_centre]
  amount_field: actual
  tolerance: 0.01
  left_label: report
  right_label: ledger
steps: [match, group, reason, draft, validate, review, record, publish]
pause_before: [review, publish]
group_by: [account]
reasoning:
  reasoner: llm
  tools: [gl.journal_lines, documents.list_documents, documents.read_pdf]
  skill: |
    Say why the report and the ledger differ for each account, from the journal
    lines and the business's documents. Cite only figures from the tools.
review: { roles: [YOUR_REVIEWER_ROLE] }
publish:
  tool: documents.render_pdf_report
  per: case
  args: { entity: $case.entity, name: $case_id, title: Report validation, subtitle: $subject,
          sections: $approved, sign_off: $sign_off }
  approver_roles: [YOUR_APPROVER_ROLE]
